subject: the scope of jlens.JacobianLens.merge()

what_merge_is_for.source: jlens/lens.py line 106 at the registered commit 581d398613e5602a5af361e1c34d3a92ea82ba8e
what_merge_is_for.docstring: Combine lenses fitted on disjoint prompt subsets into one (n_prompts-weighted mean of the inputs).
what_merge_is_for.legitimate_use: recombining shards of a SINGLE fit that were computed on different GPUs for speed

permitted: shards of half A -> merge() -> lens_A
shards of half B -> merge() -> lens_B
forbidden: any operation equivalent to it, including averaging their Jacobians by hand or fitting a single lens over A and B together and calling the result either name

why_this_is_written_as_an_explicit_ban.the_danger: merge() would accept lens_A and lens_B without complaint. They agree on source_layers and d_model, so the ValueError guards do not fire. The call would succeed and return a perfectly well-formed lens.
why_this_is_written_as_an_explicit_ban.the_consequence: every cross-fit stability criterion would then be comparing a lens against itself. C4 would pass trivially, and the P-4 feature screen that requires a feature to clear the band under BOTH lenses would lose its entire meaning.
why_this_is_written_as_an_explicit_ban.why_that_is_worse_than_a_crash: the failure is silent. Nothing raises, no test fails, and the resulting numbers look normal - they simply no longer measure what they claim to measure.
why_this_is_written_as_an_explicit_ban.hence: the ban is registered explicitly rather than left to be inferred from the docstring

what_the_independence_is_for: C4, the cross-fit agreement criterion of OD-009
the P-4 requirement that a feature clear the band under both the A and the B lens
the P-4 rank-correlation floor on JA across the two lenses
claim_ceiling: This is a procedural prohibition. It licenses no claim of any kind.
